correctness.rationale: For every integer \(p,q\ge1\) and every real \(h\ge0\), orthogonal Laplacian projectors give five rational entry classes. Three off-diagonal classes factor as strictly positive expressions at \(h>0\). \(F(x)=2(3-x)/(x^2+4x+6)\) has global minimum \((5-3\sqrt3)/2\), and the projector diagonal bound is strictly positive through \(N=11\). For every \(N\ge12\) the explicit choice \(h=8/\max(p,q)\) makes a diagonal in the smaller part negative by the exact identity delta=-5/51+C(w)/N and \(20/17-C(w)=4(32w^2+40w+53)/[51(32w^2+80w+51)]>0\). Continuity and T_h -> all-ones/N prove small-step and large-step recovery. The actual packaged verify.py independently passed 7 symbolic identities and 228 exact-rational full matrix comparisons. Finite checks are supplemental, not an infinite proof.

value.rationale: Complete bipartite graphs are a natural infinite diffusion graph class spanning stars and dense balanced graphs; the theorem pins down a sharp order-only boundary at \(N=11\) versus \(N=12\) independently of the part sizes. For every larger graph it explicitly identifies a negative entry at a concrete step and proves eventual positivity recovery, an important nuance for high-order Runge–Kutta mass-preserving diffusion. This classification is not a tautological stability-function substitution, not restricted to arbitrary hand-picked graph slices, and is not implied by the existing star-only result. It does not claim all positivity interval endpoints.
